The optimization notes are split across these pages:

- [Critical Points and Optimality Conditions](optimization-critical-points.qmd):
  flat points and critical points, Fermat's theorem, Taylor approximations, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
  and the first- and second-order conditions in several variables. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
- [Convexity in Several Variables](optimization-convexity.qmd):
  convex sets and functions, epigraphs, tangent planes, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
  and the first-order and Hessian characterizations of convexity. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
- [Quadratic Minimization under Linear Constraints](optimization-constrained.qmd):
  minimization problems, optimization algorithms, the Lagrangian, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
  and the sensitivity of the minimum to the constraints. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
- [Newton's Method](optimization-newton.qmd):
  iterative methods, the quadratic model, and quadratic convergence. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
- [Gradient Descent](optimization-gradient-descent.qmd):
  descent directions, line search, step lengths, and the failure modes <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
  of gradient descent on the Rosenbrock function, double wells, and plateaus. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
- [Quasi-Newton Methods](optimization-quasi-newton.qmd):
  the secant condition, the BFGS update, and L-BFGS. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

A link to a section, theorem or definition on this page from before the split
goes on to the page that now holds it.

## Further reading {#sec-additional-resources}

- @boyd2004convex
  is the standard reference on convex optimization, covering convex sets, convex functions, convex optimization problems, duality, unconstrained minimization, and interior-point methods.
- @nocedal2006numerical
  is a comprehensive reference on continuous numerical optimization, covering line search methods, trust-region methods, conjugate gradient methods, quasi-Newton methods, and nonlinear equations.
- [M/CS 335, Linear Optimization](https://catalog.wwu.edu/preview_course_nopop.php?catoid=23&coid=126769)
  at Western Washington University
  covers optimizing linear functions under linear constraints, including linear programming and duality.
- [M/CS 375, Numerical Computation](https://catalog.wwu.edu/preview_course_nopop.php?catoid=23&coid=126770)
  at Western Washington University
  is a further course on computing numerical answers by computer.
- [Hua Zhou](https://hua-zhou.github.io/)'s [course page for "UCLA Biostat 257 - Statistical Computing" (2025 Spring)](https://ucla-biostat-257.github.io/2025spring/)
  has lectures on optimization, from root finding to constrained problems.
  Its source is [on GitHub](https://github.com/ucla-biostat-257/2025spring) under the MIT License.
- [Hua Zhou](https://hua-zhou.github.io/)'s [lecture notes for "UCLA Biostat 216 - Mathematical Methods for Biostatistics" (2024 Fall)](https://ucla-biostat-216.github.io/2024fall/slides/13-optim/13-optim.html)
- [Neural Networks](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLZHQObOWTQDNU6R1_67000Dx_ZCJB-3pi)
  is a YouTube playlist by Grant Sanderson (3Blue1Brown);
  its chapters on gradient descent and backpropagation calculus visually illustrate
  how gradients of multivariate cost functions are computed and used for optimization.
